notes: SA's largest independent payment provider. Card machines: Yoco Go (R599), Yoco Khumo (R699), Yoco Neo (R1499), Yoco Counter+Neo Touch (R2999). Raised $83M Series C (2021). 250K+ merchant base predominantly in retail, hospitality, and services.

Acquired by Standard Bank in 2014. QR-code-based payments — no card machine required. Popular in restaurants, markets, pop-up stores, and events. Available on iOS and Android. Competes directly with Yoco for the SME hospitality segment.

Acquired by DPO Group (2021), then Network International (2022). South Africa's most widely used online gateway. Supports 20+ payment methods including instant EFT, credit/debit cards, Mobicred, and Zapper. Critical for e-commerce merchants with Takealot Marketplace integration.

Focused on developer-friendly API-first approach. Serves medium-to-large SA merchants including Superbalist, OneDayOnly, and hospitality chains. Supports 3D Secure 2.0, tokenisation, and recurring billing. Growing rapidly in the B2B SaaS vertical.

One of South Africa's oldest payment gateways (est. 2000). Acquired by DPO Group. Serves enterprise merchants including large retailers, travel agencies, and government e-services. Strong in recurring billing and subscription management. Complementary to PayFast in the DPO portfolio.
